answer: Context-forged spiral keying.** Each agent must derive its identity key by iterating a keyed hash over its own signed interaction transcript until a rare saffron-grade digest (144-bit pattern) appears. The transcript binds identity to a verifiable history, so copying a key forces replaying its entire spiral, which the protocol rejects as a duplicate context sequence. Attackers can forge a batch of keys only by first generating distinct real transcripts costing real interaction work per identity.
